refresh_policy.rationale: Collection reads the JSON that www.perplexity.ai serves the owner's own signed-in session, through the page's own fetch. Perplexity shows a Cloudflare human check on signed-in pages, so the owner may need to complete it before collection continues. A valid session refreshes without a prompt; the first run and an expired session need the owner to sign in through the browser handoff.

streams.name: conversations
streams.description: Threads (question-and-answer conversations) in the owner's Perplexity library. One record per thread, keyed by Perplexity's stable thread context uuid.

display.label: Your Perplexity threads
display.detail: Each thread in your library: title, search mode, model, last activity time, entry count and access level. Questions and answers are the separate messages stream.

id.description: The thread's context uuid, stable across renames and new answers.

title.description: The thread title Perplexity shows in the library. Null when the thread has none yet.

slug.description: The URL slug of the thread's latest entry, which addresses the thread page. Null when the list did not carry one.

mode.description: The search mode the thread ran in (web, academic, writing, ...).

model.description: The display model that answered, as the library shows it.

create_time.description: When the thread was created, taken from its first entry's creation time while the thread's entries are being read. Null on a conversations-only run or when the thread has no readable entry, because the list endpoint carries no creation time.

update_time.description: The thread's last activity (its last query time), the stream's cursor.

entry_count.description: The number of question-and-answer entries Perplexity reports for the thread.

access.description: The thread's access level code as the library carries it.

streams.name: messages
streams.description: The questions and answers inside each Perplexity thread. Every entry becomes two records: the user's question and the assistant's answer, including the citations the answer used.

display.label: Your Perplexity messages
display.detail: Each question you asked and each answer Perplexity gave, with the model, the time, and the web citations behind the answer.

id.description: The entry's uuid with the role appended: <entry uuid>:user or <entry uuid>:assistant.

conversation_id.description: The thread's context uuid, matching a conversations record.

content.description: The question text, or the answer's full markdown. Null when the entry carried none.

create_time.description: For a question, its entry's creation time; for an answer, the entry's last update time, which is when the answer finished.

model.description: The model that produced the answer. Null on a question.

citations.description: The web results the answer cited: [{ title, url }]. Empty for questions.

reason_display_messages.covered_in_full: All Perplexity threads in the selected time range have already been collected.
reason_display_messages.collection_interrupted: Perplexity stopped answering partway through, so some threads are missing. The next run continues from where this one stopped.
reason_display_messages.nothing_in_range: There are no Perplexity threads in the selected time range.
reason_display_messages.records_unreadable: Some threads in your Perplexity library couldn't be read and were skipped — everything else was collected normally.
reason_display_messages.sign_in_required: Perplexity needs you to sign in (and pass its human check) before this can continue.
reason_display_messages.source_limit_reached: This run reached a Perplexity limit. The next run will retry the remaining threads.
reason_display_messages.source_unreadable: Perplexity answered with a shape this connector doesn't recognise, so nothing more was read. Perplexity may have changed its site — please report this rather than retrying.
